newsitem.title: USA: Nuevo Energy tests positive on Texas, Calif wells.
newsitem.headline: Nuevo Energy tests positive on Texas, Calif wells.

text.p: Nuevo Energy Co, a Houston-based oil exploration and development company, said Wednesday that it had tested positive for oil in one of its California wells and for gas and oil in two Texas wells which are part of the promising Austin Chalk formation.

The company said its Bardsdale exploration well, the Irwin-Berylwood 8, located in Ventura County, California, tested at a rate of 1,241 barrels per day of 33.8 degree API (American Petroleum Institute) oil.
"Nuevo expects sustainable production to average between 500 to 600 (barrels per day). Nuevo is the operator and owns a 98% net revenue interest in the well," the company said in a statement.

In Texas, the Jolly 1-H well located in the Giddings Field on Nuevo's 1,180 acre Mancuso Prospect tested at an initial rate of 19.1 million cubic feet of gas per day and 35 barrels of condensate per day from the Austin Chalk formation on a 25/64 inch choke with a flowing tubing pressure of 5,000 pounds per square inch.

This single lateral horizontal well was drilled with an extension of 3,665 feet. Nuevo owns a 51 percent working interest in this well. Union Pacific Resources Company as operator, owns a 20.41 percent working interest, Adams Resources and Energy, Inc. owns a 13.3 percent working interest and the remaining working interest is privately held.

Also, the No. 1 Maximus well, an exploratory well located in Fayette County, Texas was horizontally drilled and completed as a dual-lateral in the Austin Chalk formation. The well tested at a rate of 1,207 barrels of oil per day and 2.0 million cubic feet of gas per day through open hole intervals at 11,663 - 15,326 ft. and 12,216 - 14,461 ft. Flowing tubing pressure was 1,925 pounds per square inch through a 22/64 inch choke.
Nuevo owns a 25 percent working interest in this well which is operated by Arrow Exploration Company.
